body: Turns out, music might be the secret ingredient According to a 2026 study from the University of Copenhagen, researchers found that smooth, harmonious music with higher notes can make sweet drinks taste sweeter, while sharp, dissonant sounds can intensify sour flavors. Using brain scans, researchers observed how different sounds influenced activity in regions associated with taste and touch, suggesting that flavor isn’t just determined by your taste buds.

source_caption_text:
Turns out, music might be the secret ingredient 👀

According to a 2026 study from the University of Copenhagen, researchers found that smooth, harmonious music with higher notes can make sweet drinks taste sweeter, while sharp, dissonant sounds can intensify sour flavors. Using brain scans, researchers observed how different sounds influenced activity in regions associated with taste and touch, suggesting that flavor isn’t just determined by your taste buds. It’s an experience your brain creates using multiple senses.

(📸: GETTY)
